$comment: TEMPLATE FILE — read the top-level README.md shipped next to this file's own template before editing. This hook blocks a Claude Code session from committing directly to main/master. It is git-tracked, so no per-checkout install step is needed — unlike a real .git/hooks/pre-commit, which requires a `cp` per checkout and reliably lags days-to-never behind bootstrap. Two limits on how automatic that is, both from Claude Code's own hooks documentation (workspace-trust section, fetched 2026-09-24) rather than inferred: in an INTERACTIVE session hooks from every settings file are held back until you accept the workspace-trust dialog for the folder (or for a parent directory whose trust extends to it); in a `-p`/SDK session the dialog is never shown and the folder is treated as trusted, so a committed hook runs immediately. And in neither case does this touch a human typing `git commit` in a terminal — it is a PreToolUse hook on the agent's tool calls, and `git init` installs no git hook (verified: a shell commit on main exits 0). Two edge cases, both handled explicitly rather than left to fail open: (1) a brand-new repo's unborn HEAD, before any commit exists — `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` errors on this and would leave the branch check silently unable to fire; fixed by using `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` instead, which resolves the branch name correctly in both the unborn and normal case. (2) this project isn't a git repository at all yet (e.g. this template was copied into a plain folder before `git init` ran) — rather than silently allow (the gate simply can't reason about branches with no repo, so doing nothing would look like protection while providing none), this asks for explicit confirmation with a visible warning instead, on the principle that a gate whose failure mode is silent is not proven until it's been made to fail loudly. Extend the same PreToolUse array with further checks (e.g. a review-artifact-required-before-merge gate) as this project's own workflow needs them -- APPEND them rather than prepending, because .claude/hooks/selftest-branch-guard.sh reads the first "Bash"-matcher group and would otherwise report a confusing red against a perfectly good gate; each new BINDING rule you add here should ship with this kind of mechanical check in the same change, or be labeled advisory instead. Known sharp edge, confirmed live in dogfooding: this check reads the branch you're on BEFORE the whole Bash command runs, so `git switch feature-x && git commit ...` in one call is denied against your old branch even though the commit would have landed correctly on the new one after the switch — run the switch as its own command first, never chained onto the commit.

hooks.command: jq -r '.tool_input.command' | { read -r cmd; if echo "$cmd" | grep -qE '(^|[;&|]\s*)git\s+commit\b'; then if ! git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"ask","permissionDecisionReason":"WARNING: branch-protection gate inactive \u2014 this is not a git repository yet (no .git found), so this hook cannot check anything. Run git init before your first commit if you want main/master protection; proceeding now commits with no branch discipline in effect."}}'; exit 0; fi; branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null); if [ "$branch" = "main" ] || [ "$branch" = "master" ]; then echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"BLOCKED: direct commit to main/master. Create a feature branch first."}}'; exit 0; fi; fi; }
